deep.reconstruction:
This page is a pictorial check of the formalism set up on the previous page. That formalism encodes a finite stratified space as a family of manifolds with boundary V_i^0 indexed by a finite poset I. Each V_i^0 is the stratum with open tubular neighbourhoods of lower strata removed. The boundary of V_i^0 decomposes into pieces ∂_j V_i^0 (j<i), and each piece fibres over V_j^0. The page works out the simplest examples.

(1) I={0}: V_0 is a point, a closed manifold.

(2) I={0<1}: the line with a marked point. Removing a small open interval around the point gives V_1, two closed half-lines. Its boundary is ∂V_1 = V_{1,0}, two points. The diagram ∂V_1 = V_{10} → V_0 (fibration with fibre S^0), with ∂V_1 ↓ V_1 (inclusion of the boundary), is the gluing datum. One recovers the original space as V_1 ∪_{V_{10}} (mapping cylinder of V_{10}→V_0).

(3) I={0<1<2}: the plane V_2 containing a line V_1 through a point V_0. Removing tubular neighbourhoods gives the hatched V_2, a manifold with corners. Its boundary has two kinds of pieces:
- ∂_1V_2 = V_{21}: the lines parallel to V_1, i.e. four half-lines. This is an S^0-bundle over V_1 (fibre without boundary, since 1 is a predecessor of 2).
- ∂_0V_2 = V_{20}: the two arcs around V_0. This is the circle minus two open intervals, fibred over the point V_0, with fibre a manifold with boundary.
- The corners V_{210} are four points. They are simultaneously ∂(∂_0V_2), ∂(∂_1V_2), and the restriction ∂_1V_2 | ∂V_1 (fibre 2 points over 2 points gives 4 points).

This verifies the formula from the previous page: ∂(∂_jV_i) = ⋃_{k<j} ∂_jV_i|∂_kV_j ∪ ∂_{i/j}V_i, with the last term empty when j is a predecessor of i. It also verifies the identification of 'bords communs' ∂_{20} ← ∂_{210} → ∂_{21}.

The point of the exercise is Grothendieck's programme of 'topologie modérée'. A tame stratified space should be equivalent to purely differential-topological combinatorial data: manifolds with corners plus compatible boundary fibrations, i.e. a resolution or 'dévissage' of the stratification. The next page pushes this to a combinatorial classification in dimensions ≤2 using finite sets, Z/2-torsors and groupoids.
errors: No mathematical error. The pictures are consistent with the formulas on p.42: |V_{210}| = 4 = |∂V_{21}| = |∂V_{20}| = |V_{21}|∂V_1|.
Minor: the labels V_{20} for both arcs and V_{21} for all four half-lines conflate a space with its connected components. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Resolving a stratified space into manifolds with boundary/corners (complements of tubular neighbourhoods of lower strata), with boundary faces fibring over lower strata, glued along common corners.
ideas.modern_name: Manifolds with fibred corners / iterated fibration structures; 'unfolding' (dépliage) of Thom–Mather stratified spaces; Thom–Mather control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969) and Mather (1970) for control data; Verona (1984) for resolutions; Melrose and Albin–Leichtman–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012) for the equivalence of Thom–Mather spaces with manifolds with fibred corners; Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi for unfoldings
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures into 'variétés à bord' with fibrations, 'théorème de dévissage'). The detailed 1974 formalism is not published.

ideas.modern_name: Codimension-2 corner faces of a manifold with fibred corners and the compatibility of iterated boundary fibrations

missed.claim: As early as 1974, Grothendieck's tame-topology notes formalize stratified spaces as poset-indexed systems of manifolds with corners whose boundary faces fibre over lower strata, with iterated corner compatibilities. This is essentially the 'manifold with fibred corners / iterated fibration structure' picture later developed independently in analysis on singular spaces (Melrose, ALMP 2012) and in the unfolding theory of intersection cohomology. The 1974 date and the explicit corner indexing ∂_{j>k>l}, predating Esquisse by ten years, are not recorded in that literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical attribution. It shows that Grothendieck's dévissage of tame spaces coincides with the resolution formalism now standard for index theory on stratified spaces. It also suggests that his combinatorial classification (next pages) could be read as a classification of iterated fibration structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only illustrative pictures of a formalism whose spirit Grothendieck himself announced in Esquisse §5 and which is now standard as manifolds with fibred corners. The early 1974 date and explicit corner bookkeeping are a modest historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Top label reads 'V_0' with a small superscript mark (likely V_0^0 or V_0^•), not just '·V_0'.
The first figure's labels are V_1^0 (left) and V_1^× or V_1^0 (right), with superscripts. The equation is '∂V_1^0 = V_{1,0}' (superscript on V_1), not plain ∂V_1.
In the right diagram the vertical arrow goes from V_{10} down to V_1 (inclusion of the boundary); the transcription is correct in content.
